posts.title: Cultural Appropriation Controversies: From Bakery Debates to Pop Stars
posts.script: August 28, 2026: the exact moment a viral Edmonton bakery feud blew up the entire internet. Quick context: this is the cultural appropriation controversies drama explained, and the timeline goes way back. Back in 2013, Katy Perry reportedly faced massive backlash for her geisha-inspired American Music Awards performance. Then in June 2019, Kim Kardashian allegedly sparked global outrage by naming her new shapewear line Kimono, forcing a quick rebrand to SKIMS. Then in 2021, Justin Bieber posted photos of blonde dreadlocks, instantly reigniting fierce debates over Black hairstyle exploitation. But the comments found something worse. Fast forward to August 28, 2026, when Better Baker owner Vinny Rozhdestvensky posted a reply viewed over 3.6 million times over a bánh mì croissant. Then just days later on September 4, Blackpink's Lisa dropped a music video that sparked separate design theft accusations from a Syrian artist. Right now, creators are still debating where online inspiration crosses the line into exploitation. So whose side are you on? Full dated timeline on GenZHype dot com.
